# A capped tab header title keeps its ellipsis after the strip has room again

## Context

Found by the operator's manual walk of `apps/workstation` on the v13.3.1 candidate (`dev` 0ab667195e), 2026-10-23 ~20:00Z, in a popup window (320 × 240 CSS px) holding two panes: the *Commits* tab's title read **"Com…"** and stayed truncated once the strip had room again. His word: minor, not release-blocking; no milestone. Recorded on #20022 as a walk finding.

Live reads through the Neural Link at 20:06Z, before anything was touched:

- `neo-tab-header-button-38` (text `Commits`, window `1be55d31…`): `maxWidth: 61`, `cls` carries `neo-tab-overflow-capped`.
- Its toolbar `neo-tab-header-toolbar-23`: rect x 0–320, 33 px tall. The button's rect: x 0–61.
- The focus-gated action rail (lock, reload, maximize, close) sits at the strip's right end; between the button's right edge and the rail roughly 160 px of strip are empty (the operator's screenshot, same moment).
- The main window carries the same state on `neo-tab-header-button-16` (`Metrics`, `maxWidth: 52`, capped) in the 14 %-extent right zone; whether that cap is currently correct was not measured.

Observation: a plugin-installed cap stayed on a button whose strip had room for its natural width. Inference, not yet traced: which room change failed to re-run the cap decision (the rail's reveal/withdraw, or the popup's resize).

## The Problem

`src/tab/plugin/Overflow.mjs` caps a protected button (the active or the focused one) that is wider than the strip's `usable` width, by writing the public `maxWidth` config and adding `neo-tab-overflow-capped` (`applySplit`, the `appliedCaps` ledger), and `resources/scss/src/tab/header/Button.scss` turns the covered cut into an ellipsis under that class. The cap clears only inside `applySplit`, when `needsCap` is false on a later projection; the plugin's own docblock states the intent: "clearing restores the exact caller value recorded at cap time". A cap is meant to be transient, and here it was not.

What the operator did between the cap and the room is the reproducer's first step; the two candidate room changes are a popup resize (the toolbar's own box changes, a resize should re-project) and the focus-gated rail withdrawing or revealing (the strip's room for tabs changes without the toolbar box changing). The hover-reveal mode (#20011) reserves the revealed cluster's width up front precisely so a hover never re-partitions; the focus-gated mode has no such reservation, so a cap computed beside the revealed rail may simply never be revisited once the rail goes.

## The Architectural Reality

- `Overflow#applySplit` (`src/tab/plugin/Overflow.mjs`, the `needsCap` branch and its mirror `else if (me.appliedCaps?.has(button.id))`): the only writer and the only clearer of the cap; `usable` comes from the caller (`project()`).
- The measurement window restores a capped button's recorded `maxWidth` before measuring, so the natural-width cache is not poisoned by the cap (the `cappedButtons` block above `applySplit`).
- Re-projection triggers: the toolbar's resize (`onResize`) and `activeIndexChange`. The rail is `tab/header` flat actions (#17418), revealed on focus, with the hold added by #20052.
- Precedents: #16424 (the cap's origin: the active tab never runs beneath the floating control), #19982 (a partition measured from visual rects inside a FLIP stayed stale until the next activation; same shape, different trigger), #18410 (a cap spec retired when the heavy header stopped staging a cap).

Design authority: the Overflow plugin's own contract, a plugin-installed cap is cleared by the plugin when the room returns.

## The Fix

1. Name the missing trigger with a setter trace on the capped button's `maxWidth` and on the rail's reveal/withdraw during the operator's sequence (the method that found #20075's writer).
2. Make the cap's lifetime follow the room: re-run the partition (or at least the cap decision for ledger members) whenever the strip's usable width changes, the rail's reveal and withdraw included, not only on a toolbar resize; or compute `usable` from the live layout rect at decision time and let the next projection clear it. Keep the hover mode's no-repartition rule (#20011) intact: its reservation already makes the hover width-neutral.
3. The control arm stays true: while the room is genuinely short (a 320-px popup with the rail revealed and a title wider than the room), the cap stays.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: A red-first Neural Link e2e under `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/`: a pane popped out into a 320-px-wide window, its title capped (`neo-tab-overflow-capped` present, `maxWidth` below the natural width); after the room returns, in two arms (the popup widened by 200 px; the focus moved so the rail withdraws), the button carries no `neo-tab-overflow-capped` class and `maxWidth` is back to the caller's value within one projection. Red on `dev` 0ab667195e for whichever arm reproduces the operator's sequence.
- [ ] AC-2: A unit arm on the plugin: a `usable` that grows past the natural width on the next projection clears the ledger entry and the class (the restore branch), and a `usable` that stays short keeps them (the control).
- [ ] AC-3: The main window's `Metrics` cap in the right zone is measured in the PR: if its room is genuinely short it stays and is recorded as correct; if it is the same residue, the fix covers it.
- [ ] AC-4 (post-merge): the operator repeats his sequence on the merged head and the title re-expands.

## Out of Scope

The hover-reveal mode's reservation and its no-repartition rule (#20011); the overflow control's own placement; #20080 (post-destroy config writes), a different class of residue.
